..
As of 210 AM Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Numerous showers and thunderstorms with areas of 
heavy rainfall remain possible today, with the greatest chance from 
our southwest sections NE to the Triad and Triangle regions and 
along the Virginia border. This will lead to a risk of isolated 
flooding.

Confidence is increasing in the potential for heavy downpours within 
showers and storms today. The current mid level pattern features a 
weak closed low over GA, while an offshore-centered anticyclone 
extends ESE toward the Southeast coast, and the westerlies remain 
displaced well to our N. This is leading to a steady SSE-to-NNW flow 
of moist and perturbed mid level flow across central NC, which will 
persist today through tonight as the low drifts N toward far SW NC.
At the surface, a nearly stationary frontal zone stretches from the 
FL Panhandle across GA, the NC Foothills, and south-central and 
eastern VA. This front is likely to waver today as it succumbs to 
the whims of convective outflows and subtle mid level disturbances, 
but overall it should remain near or just NW of our N and W CWA 
borders today/tonight. That keeps us in the warm sector, with a 
plume of high PW (130%-140% of normal), especially over eastern and 
northern sections this afternoon and evening, with the high-PW area 
shifting N into VA overnight. While fairly high cloud cover for much 
of the day will curb insolation amidst mid level lapse rates mostly 
under 6 C/km, even modest heating of an already-muggy low level 
depth will still favor CAPE of 750-1500 J/kg, with minor waves aloft 
riding over our area supporting above-climo coverage of showers and 
storms today.

In addition to the high PW and bouts of weak dynamic forcing for 
ascent, other factors will exist which will favor a risk of 
localized flooding rains. These include a high warm-cloud (LCL-0C) 
depth of 4-4.5 km (favoring efficient warm rain processes), a 
somewhat slow cell motion (expected to be under 15 kts), possible 
training cells, and an added focus for ascent provided by outflows 
and confluent flow along the low-mid level shear axis, likely to be 
oriented SW-to-NE through the CWA, roughly from near CLT to near 
IXA. The recent rain surplus has also led to damp or nearly 
saturated soils (rainfall at GSO/FAY/RDU in the last two weeks is 
200%-300% of normal). Will not issue a flood watch at this time, due 
to the expected limited coverage of the heavy downpours and the 
lingering uncertainty regarding exactly where the heavy rain might 
be focused. But if localized heavy rain does fall as expected, in 
particular over urban areas and highways, flood advisories or 
warnings may still be needed. 

The severe weather risk is fairly low today due to the clouds and 
unimpressive CAPE and bulk shear, but a few of the strongest cells, 
particularly in our southwest, could generate pulse microbursts with 
straight-line winds over 40 kts this afternoon through early evening.


KEY MESSAGE 2... Daily scattered showers and thunderstorms are 
expected to continue for the next 7 days, mainly each afternoon 
through evening.

We're likely to stay within a weak flow pattern through early next 
week, with weak but persist low level flow sourced from the Atlantic 
and Gulf. The mid level low will continue to weaken as it lifts 
through far E TN/KY and gets caught up in the westerlies 
(specifically, broad troughing over the N Plains and N Great Lakes) 
through mid-late week, while the offshore ridge strengthens and 
drifts back W toward the Mid Atlantic coast, pushing the surface 
frontal zone well back to our NW and resulting in gradually rising 
heights over NC, especially in the E by the weekend. The flat Great 
Lakes trough will weaken, but a baggy mid level trough will hold 
from Ontario down through the Ohio Valley and lower Miss Valley into 
early next week. Pops are likely to stay on the high side, good 
chance to likely, through mid week, generally higher in the NW and 
SE (the latter from sea breeze action). But as that retrograding 
ridge builds into NC, we should trend to more typical chance pops 
for Fri through Mon. The risk of widespread severe weather appears 
low overall through the forecast, but some AI models do suggest a 
trend toward few stronger storms Sat into Mon and beyond. Regarding 
temps, highs will be a bit below normal and lows a bit above normal 
today and Wed, followed by above normal highs/lows by a category or 
two Thu into the weekend.
